[CC BY-SA 4.0](https://creativecommons.org/licenses/by-sa/4.0/legalcode.en).
Project source code retains MIT. The [complete legal text](COPYING), fixed
article links, full histories, contributor records and modification notices
accompany the proposals.

Exact membership and both unchanged frequency strings derive from Boris New
and Christophe Pallier’s [Lexique 3.83](https://chrplr.github.io/openlexicon/datasets-info/Lexique383/README-Lexique.html),

and order. CEFR remains unknown.

notation is retained; `chevalier` keeps its recorded optional-schwa notation.

and liaison excluded, and retains the obligatory construction.

retain all fields and selected/excluded uses. `pars/NOM` has no proposed sense
and four unresolved fields.

and the full paginated named registry plus returned anonymous count in
[source-context.json](source-context.json). The registry may extend past the
fixed revision and is article attribution, not proof of selected-sentence

# Selected rights: #143 author proposal

The author proposes CC BY-SA 4.0 for the retained Wiktionnaire lexical and
grammar contributions, the scoped French adaptations and new EN/ZH explanations.
Fixed versions, selected spans and per-field modification notices are in
[source-excerpts.json](source-excerpts.json), [field-review.json](field-review.json)
and [rights.json](rights.json). Source-specific import/reference markers and
complete named/anonymous article credits are in [source-context.json](source-context.json).
Article attribution does not prove individual selected-sentence authorship.

## Original works

Where an article declares `Import:DAF8`, retain separate credit to Académie
française, Dictionnaire de l’Académie française, eighth edition (1932–1935).
The [established original-work review](../issue-129/selected-rights.md) applies
[L123-3](https://www.legifrance.gouv.fr/loda/article_lc/LEGIARTI000006278941/2026-02-20)
to the collective edition: using final 1935 publication yields seventy years
from 1936-01-01, conservatively expiring 2006-01-01. This concerns the original
collective work; it does not transfer rights in new Wiktionnaire or Lexique
contributions, review any new #143 field or authorize referenced literary/news
quotations. Import declarations identify the edition, not selected-sentence
authorship. The new selected-span and original-boundary records remain pending
separate review.

## Actual selected boundaries

The proposals use lexical definitions, French/POS/inflection frames and applicable
IPA only. `chevalier` selects the explicitly contemporary order-member subsense,
not the ancient or medieval referent. `mexicain/NOM` selects the lowercase language
noun, not capitalized inhabitants. `uns/PRO:ind` binds to the explicit `les uns`
plural table and the contrastive group sense of `l’un`; the separate partitive
`l’un de` sense explicitly requires `quelques-uns` in the plural and is excluded.
The /œ̃/ IPA is the recorded plural pronoun segment of `le.z‿œ̃`, with article and
liaison excluded. `jusque` retains its construction restriction and does not add
an alias for `jusqu’à`. `pars/NOM` stays unresolved; the singular golf approval
for frozen row 128 grants no exception to row 3128.

Reference lists, external dictionary titles and article-level labels do not
license unselected prose. Literary/news quotations, media, audio, other-language
text and etymology supply no learner field. Raw articles remain outside the
repository as research captures; tracked selected material contains no example
quotation bodies.

## Authorities and obligations

The archive retains the actual CC BY-SA 4.0 legal text, Wikimedia Terms section
7 and fixed French copyright/import policies with their original capture metadata
and reuse chain. The author read the selected licensing provisions. CC sections
2(a), 3(a), 3(b) and 4 permit the licensed sharing/adaptation/database route with
attribution, source/licence and warranty identification, modification notices,
ShareAlike and no downstream restrictions. Public-domain original work remains
separate. Wikimedia section 7 permits linked article/history attribution and
requires imported-source conditions and prior modifications to remain visible.

[NOTICES.md](NOTICES.md) and [COPYING](COPYING) provide author-stage notices and
legal text. No new field has independent quality or rights acceptance. Actual
combined redistribution materials, conversion and native checks remain with the
coordinator. Original-work credit, full contributor/history links, fixed source
versions, selected material and modification notices must accompany admitted
content; adaptations retain CC BY-SA 4.0. Project source code remains MIT.
